3.happening: We sort nums so equal values sit next to each other.
3.why: Sorting lets us recognise and skip duplicate triples cheaply later.
3.invariant: The multiset of numbers is unchanged; only their order changed.

4.happening: We record n = {n}, the count of numbers.
4.why: All three loops need the end boundary.
4.invariant: n never changes for the rest of the search.

5.happening: We start result as an empty list.
5.why: It will collect only the unique triples that sum to zero.
5.invariant: No triple has been accepted yet.

6.happening: Anchor index i moves to {i}, the first number of the triple.
6.why: Fixing i lets the inner loops search every pair after it.
6.invariant: Every triple starting before i has already been considered.

7.happening: Index j moves to {j}, the second number, always after i.
7.why: Starting j after i keeps the three indices distinct and avoids repeats.

8.happening: Index k sweeps to {k}, the third number, always after j.
8.why: k scans every remaining position to complete the triple.
8.invariant: i < j < k is always true.

9.happening: We add the three highlighted values into total.
9.why: A triple qualifies only when its three values sum to zero.
9.invariant: total describes exactly the currently highlighted i, j, k.

10.happening: total is {total} — the three values cancel to zero.
10.why: This is exactly the condition for a valid triple.
10.invariant: A zero-sum triple has been located at i, j, k.

10.happening: total is {total}, not zero, so this triple is rejected.
10.why: Only triples summing to zero are answers.
10.invariant: No stored triple is affected by a rejected candidate.

11.happening: We build the concrete triple from nums[i], nums[j], nums[k].
11.why: We need the values (not indices) to compare against what we already stored.
11.invariant: triple holds the three values that just summed to zero.

12.happening: result is still empty, so this triple is new.
12.why: The first zero-sum triple is always worth keeping.
12.invariant: Only distinct triples are ever stored.

12.happening: We check whether this triple was already collected.
12.why: Sorting can produce the same triple from different indices; we keep each once.
12.invariant: result never holds two identical triples.

13.happening: We append the new triple {triple} to result.
13.why: It is a distinct set of three numbers that sum to zero.
13.invariant: result now contains this triple exactly once.

14.happening: We return result with {len(result)} unique triple(s).
14.why: Every combination of three indices has been tested.
14.invariant: result holds every distinct zero-sum triple.

init.happening: Sort the array and prepare an empty answer list.
init.why: Setup for an exhaustive, duplicate-free triple search.
init.invariant: No triple has been accepted yet.

loop.happening: Advance one of the three triple cursors.
loop.why: Nested loops enumerate every combination i < j < k.
loop.invariant: The three indices are always strictly increasing.

update.happening: Compute a sum or record a found triple.
update.why: Each candidate triple must be summed and possibly stored.

check.happening: Test the triple's sum or its novelty.
check.why: Only new, zero-sum triples are kept.
